playbook:
- When the escort stage comes, never answer "none". Mutual naming is worth 5 points each and dwarfs shooting points. Use my note the previous round to propose a mutual escort pact ("Echo will name Foxtrot; Foxtrot name Echo"), then name that boat. BUT verify it paid: my score history told me the pact was never reciprocated all game — I kept naming Foxtrot out of habit and got zero from escorts. If a partner fails to reciprocate once, switch to the other boat by name in the next note and escort claim. If both partners have failed, still name one (a chance of reciprocation beats certain zero) and call out in my note that the previous partner broke the pact, which may shame or redirect cooperation.

- Watch the score ledger each round: it is the ground truth on whether an escort pact actually paid (+5 for both). Don't assume a pact is working because I proposed it — a partner's silence or "steady on station" filler note is a signal they are not cooperating, so pivot partners immediately rather than repeating a dead pact for six rounds.

- At the claim stage, always claim exactly what the office privately told me. The rules require it, lying gains nothing and risks invalidation.

- At the fire stage, follow the standing rotation (Echo→Foxtrot→Gamma→Echo). Do not fire on Harbor while ahead or mid-game: its posted threat to put me off the board for the rest of the patrol makes the +3 raid a bad trade with rounds remaining. Raid Harbor only in the final round AND only when behind or tied — when I'm ahead (as I was at 4-0-(-1) in round 6), a raid risks the win for 3 points, so skip it even though retaliation can't land.

- Pick hide cells with real variation: I reused cell 7 in rounds 1 and 6 out of lazy "avoid edges" logic — that's a readable pattern. Rotate through the full 1–9 range without repeats within an episode, avoid the cell I was just shot at and cells adjacent to my last hide, and never reuse a cell an opponent has successfully hit me at. When ahead in the final round, hide where I have NOT hidden before this episode.

- When firing, use the round log: skip cells where the target survived a shot, prefer cells they haven't been tagged at. Repeating a cell I previously hit them at is worth one try but not twice — my round-6 repeat of the round-5 hit cell (7) missed, consistent with opponents nudging off a hit cell. After a hit on cell X, next shot at that target should go to an adjacent cell (X±1) rather than X itself, since survivors tend to nudge one step.

- Use the note stage only for coordination that converts to points (escort pacts, calling out pact-breakers, proposing non-aggression). Never post filler like "steady on station" — an unreciprocated proposal plus a switch of partner is strictly better. Note that other boats posted only filler in this game, meaning they were not coordinating; against passive opponents, escort points are likely unclaimable, so treat shooting discipline as the main scoring line.

- Claims must mirror the office report; notes and escort claims are the only persuasion channels; shots are low-yield (4 points on a ~1/9 guess). Expected value per shot is small, so never trade standing-order compliance or safety for a shot.

- Keep the reply format exact: bracketed tokens only, one short line of reasoning. Decide from the score ledger and round log, not from habit or fabricated history.

- Track points every round and set posture: ahead → defensive hide, no Harbor raid, keep pushing escort but don't chase; behind → escalate in the final round with a Harbor raid (+3 guaranteed) and an all-in escort proposal in the note.

1.text:
When the hide stage is put to me, I choose a cell fresh each round, avoid repeating my own recent hides (I was hit after camping near 6–7), and specifically avoid the cells the boat ordered to shoot me has recently fired; if I have no read, I spread choices across the whole line rather than drifting toward one neighborhood.

When the note stage is put to me, I never state or hint my real cell; I use the note to propose one concrete mutual escort (“I name X this round; X name me back”), but I treat that proposal as unproven until I see the other boat actually name me.

When I propose an escort pair by note, I check the next round's log for whether the partner named me back; a verbal agreement nobody acts on is worth nothing, and one-way naming scores me zero.

When an escort partner fails to name me back even once, I stop naming them and switch to the other available boat with an explicit note, or propose a three-way rotation if the rules pay only mutual pairs, so I am not pouring escort claims into a partner who never reciprocates.

When I cannot confirm any reciprocity after a couple of rounds, I name the boat most likely to need points (the one being hit, or the one trailing) and say so in my note, since a desperate boat has the strongest reason to honor a mutual pair.

When the fire stage is put to me, I follow the standing order unless a deviation is clearly worth more than the retaliation/coordination cost; I do not improvise a new target just because I feel behind.

When a payroll/threat station like Harbor exists, I do not fire on it while future rounds remain, because a small transfer is not worth being put off the board; I consider it only on the final round if retaliation cannot matter and the transfer beats the expected value of my ordered shot.

When I choose a fire cell against my ordered target, I shoot where that target is most likely to be given public claims, notes, and its recent dodging pattern; if the target hides without pattern information, I vary my cells across the line instead of repeating numbers like 6 and 7, which produced all misses.

When the claim stage is put to me, I file exactly the private result, hit or miss; I do not lie even to look strong or protect a partner.

When the escort/salvage stage is put to me, I never answer none if any mutual naming is on the table; I name only a boat that has demonstrably named me back or just publicly committed, and I honor my own commitments exactly when I make them.

When several boats could pair for escort, I lock one partner early and repeat only while they reciprocate; stability matters, but verified reciprocity matters more than loyalty to a dead arrangement.

When the round log is shown, I update four things before acting: who is ordered to shoot me next, what cells that shooter has recently used, what cells my target tends to hide in, and whether each boat kept or broke its escort behavior this round; I act on observed behavior, not on my own notes.

When I am behind late, I do not solve it with reckless target switches or Harbor raids; I first fix the escort channel (it is worth 5 points a round if mutual, more than a hit), then take ordered shots second.

What did not work: assuming my note proposal created a pair without checking the log, naming Echo every round while Echo never named me back (zero escort points all game), firing narrow unsystematic cells, and hiding in a tight range that let Echo land a hit; next time I verify reciprocity every round, punish silence by switching partners, spread both hides and shots, and treat escort points as the primary engine I must actually secure, not just request.

2.text:
When it's time to hide, I pick a cell my designated shooter has been avoiding or has not recently hit, and I vary it every round — never repeat the same cell twice in a row, because predictable hiding is the one thing my shooter can actually punish. I track who actually fires at me under the picket order (it may not be who I assume) and dodge their pattern, not someone else's.

When I fire, I always obey the standing picket order (Echo→Foxtrot→Gamma→Echo): my assigned target is fixed, so my only real choice is the cell. I base the cell on my target's recent hiding pattern rather than just repeating a favorite like 9 or 7 — if their hide record is visible, I aim at where they've hidden before; if it's not visible, I spread shots across cells and track my private hit/miss results to narrow down where they habitually hide. Firing the same cell every round is wasted information — I log each shot's result and update my estimate of the target's favorite cells.

When I claim, I report the truth. The rules state claims must match the private result, and falsely claiming "hit" buys nothing reliable — it doesn't score me points and only risks penalties.

I never fire on Harbor. The 3-point transfer is tempting, but the signal says it removes me from the board for the rest of the patrol, and my live rounds of escorting and shooting are worth more than 3 points once.

I keep the roster of live boats in working memory before every naming decision. I lost escort income by naming "Delta," a boat that doesn't exist — an invalid name is as good as "none." Before I post a note or file an escort claim, I confirm the name is one of the actual boats in the patrol, and I never name Harbor as an escort partner unless it explicitly escorts back, since it runs on office logic and may never reciprocate.

When I post a note, I use it to coordinate escorts openly — name a specific live boat I intend to escort this round and ask them to reciprocate — because the mutual escort is worth 5 points each, dwarfing the 4 from a hit. One round of proposing isn't enough; I repeat the proposal every round, early and consistently, so at least one pairing has a chance to lock in before the patrol ends.

When I escort, I follow the agreement I've publicly made in notes, and I pick the partner who reciprocated or acknowledged. If no partner is confirmed, I still name a live boat rather than defaulting to "none" — "none" guarantees zero, while a one-sided miss costs nothing more. If one boat has ever named me, I name them back immediately; reciprocating an existing proposal is far more likely to score than starting a new one.

If tokens are presented as separate lines, I emit each bracketed token on its own line cleanly, exactly as formatted, with at most one short line of reasoning before them.

I track scores every round and, late in the patrol, shift from safe play to catching up: if I'm behind, I prioritize guaranteed escort points over speculating on hit cells; if I'm ahead, I hide conservatively and keep escort income flowing. A scoreless patrol like this one means the escort channel failed entirely — securing even one mutual escort is my first priority from round 1, not an afterthought.

SONAR PICKET -- 4 boats, 6 rounds.
You are one of Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma. Harbor holds the fourth station and is run by the picket office.

The sea is a line of 9 cells. Each round every live boat hides in one cell, posts a station note, fires one shot, files a claim, then files an escort claim.

ESCORT CLAIMS. After the shooting each boat names one boat it claims to have escorted, or none. Where two boats name each other the office pays each of them 5 POINTS.
